constraint: Must maintain shoulder implant function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Radiographic monitoring of bushing wear to detect early component degradation and prevent implant malfunction.
intervention: Implement periodic radiographic surveillance of shoulder implant bearing surfaces, specifically assessing wear patterns analogous to bushing wear in the elbow prosthesis, to identify early wear before clinical failure.
expected_effect: Early detection of wear allows timely intervention (e.g., revision or bearing exchange) to maintain shoulder implant function within clinical specifications and prevent catastrophic malfunction.
falsification_test: In a retrospective cohort of shoulder implant patients, compare time-to-malfunction or revision rates between those with scheduled radiographic wear assessments (e.g., annual) and those without; if no significant difference in malfunction-free survival, the mechanism is not effective.
mechanism_source_span: "Radiographs were analyzed for component loosening, bushing wear, and periarticular ossifications."

source_evidence.source_title: Total elbow arthroplasty for unreconstructible distal humerus fracture sequelae in patients less than 40 year old. Long-term outcomes.
source_evidence.source_span: Background Total elbow arthroplasty (TEA) is rarely recommended in young patients because of a high risk of early failure. This study analyzes the long-term outcomes of a cohort of post-traumatic TEA patients under 40 years of age who received a linked semiconstrained implant to manage the sequelae of an unreconstructible distal humerus fracture.
